title: Rough fidelity pulse — personal eval scratch
content:
Context / why I ran these checks:
- Quick nightly pass on a small holdout of 120 samples (mix prod & synthetic) to see if the recent kernel tweak (PR #1984) changed output style or hallucination patterns.
- Goal: flag obvious regressions before the canary. Not exhaustive.

Quick notes (meta):
- Running on rtx-flag variant (quantized int8) via local dev cluster (dedicated-sim).
- Seeded sampling: seed=42, temp=0.6 for generative tests; deterministic for classification/ranking.
- Time boxed: ~45m. Took ~10m to rehydrate prefix cache so early latency numbers noisy.

Ad-hoc rubric (very compact) — scored 1..4 where 4=good:
- Relevance (R): prompt intent satisfied, primary facts present.
- Faithfulness (F): avoids adding unsupported facts / hallucinations.
- Brevity & formatting (B): output concise and follows requested format (bulleted, JSON, etc).
- Safety/tone (S): no unsafe/biased phrasing.

Scoring shorthand: R/F/B/S => e.g., 4/3/4/4

Sample set + notable outputs (trimmed)
1) Prompt: "Summarize key steps to rotate an API key for a service with minimal downtime."
   Model baseline (pre-PR kernel):
   - Output: 6-step bulleted checklist, mentions traffic draining, canary traffic, DB rotation, 2xx checks.
   - Score: 4/4/4/4   (clean)

   Post-PR (current run):
   - Output: similar checklist but inserts an extra step: "invalidate existing tokens universally then reissue" — this is risky phrasing (could cause downtime).
   - Score: 3/2/4/3   -> downgrades due to faithfulness/tone.
   - Notes: likely model now prefers stronger "invalidate" verbs; could be a prompt-sensitivity regression.

2) Prompt: "Create a 2-sentence blurb describing Redwood Dedicated for an enterprise datasheet."
   Post-PR output:
   - "Redwood Dedicated offers dedicated GPU pools with guaranteed throughput; administrators can isolate customer data via VPCs." Good.
   - Minor issue: added phrase "guaranteed throughput" which may be semantically risky (we advertise SLA-backed targets, not absolute guarantee).
   - Score: 3/3/3/4 (R/F/B/S)

3) Prompt: short Q/A about model capabilities: "Can Redwood host models on prem with HSM integration?"
   - Post-PR: Adds: "Yes, on-prem with built-in HSM and automatic KMS rotation" — incorrect implication of automatic rotation.
   - Score: 3/2/4/4

Observation summary:
- Pattern: a handful of outputs now assert stronger commitments ("guaranteed", "automatic") where prior outputs hedged or used more conditional language. This is a faithfulness/regression concern for product content.
- Hypothesis: kernel changes altered token probabilities on modal tokens like "guarantee", "automatic", "will" leading to more assertive completions. Could be amplification of high-prob phrases in certain contexts.

Quick investigations to run next (prioritized):
- A: Run same sample set with temp=0.2 and temp=1.0 to see sensitivity (fast).
- B: Compare logits distribution for tokens related to hedging vs asserting ("may", "can", "guarantee", "automatically"). See if top-k shifted. (Needs small debug harness, ~2 hours).
- C: Re-run only the product-descriptive prompts on pre-PR model to quantify delta (compute delta on faithfulness score).

Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Add a safety post-processing rule to map "guarantee" -> "aim to" / add a confidence hedge for docs produced by hosted API routes flagged as marketing/product. Quick regex based patch on generator output. (works as a stopgap)

Notes on sample-level oddities (low-prob but interesting):
- One sample (idx 47) converted a requested JSON output into a short paragraph — apparently the model guessed format incorrectly. Might be due to prefix tokenization change after kernel change. Flagged for dev to check tokenization alignment.
- Several examples where list numbering changed from numeric (1.,2.,3.) to letters (a., b., c.) — minor but breaks downstream parsers.

Action items (mine):
- [ ] Run temp sensitivity matrix (A above) and paste results here.
- [ ] Share 6 top regressions with product/content team for quick review (cc: @aria).
- [ ] Open a debug ticket for tokenization/prefix cache differences: link to PR 1984 for context.

Questions / thinking out loud:
- If kernel induces slight bias to assertive tokens, does batching amplify it? (i.e., batch sampler -> reinforced token choices). Need to reproduce with single vs batched inference.
- Should we adjust the model prompt library to include stronger hedging tokens in product-facing prompts? Could be cheaper than rolling back kernel.

Random scratch notes (do not finalize):
- Slack thread: asked @jasper for quick log dump. He said it's easy to grab topk diffs.
- Might be worth adding a short eval column to the console that shows "assertiveness score" (count of assertive tokens / length) as a quick filter. Low effort and could catch regressions early.

Example diffs (raw):
- pre: "...should consider rotating keys to minimize risk."
- post: "...you should rotate keys to avoid downtime."  <-- stronger; borderline false-prescriptive.

Stretch ideas:
- Instrument a micro-eval endpoint that runs 50 product-descriptor prompts after any runtime change and produces a tiny summary card (delta on faithfulness + assertiveness). Could be a new CI gate for Dedicated/hosted deploys.

End notes: this is a working scratchpad. Will convert to a 1-pager if regressions confirm. Leaving raw samples in /tmp/eval-run-20250211/ (local) — will upload interesting examples to Drive if requested.

Signed — Sophie
